status: DESCRIPTIVE PLANNING -- no hypothesis tested, nothing fitted, nothing selected, nothing in the live system changed. Sizes the news evaluation (roadmap 8.6 / J) before any news-versus-outcome figure exists.
why: Roadmap 8.6 re-opens 'does the news score carry information?' at 500 live hours with a usable news score. That number was set without a power analysis, and the news score is unusually persistent: each story stays in the 24-hour window and is re-scored ~19 times (roadmap J(a)). Before anyone looks at news against outcomes, how many hours would the planned test need to detect an effect of the size this programme has ever seen (|rho| 0.05-0.08)?
data_touched: The live news category score of every pipeline-0.2.0 hour with a usable score (97 hours, 2026-09-19 20:00 -> 2026-09-24 15:00 UTC), read from the predictions table. NO return, outcome or price was read; tests/test_news_power.py enforces this by inspecting the module's only query. The news-versus-outcome relation therefore remains unexamined, and the eventual test stays clean.
method: Two independent routes. (1) Analytic, Bartlett: under no relationship, Var(r) = (1/n) sum_k rho_x(k) rho_y(k); hourly returns are close to serially uncorrelated and an h-hour forward return overlaps its neighbours, rho_y(k) = max(0, 1-|k|/h), so the variance inflation is VIF(h) = 1 + 2 sum_{k<h} rho_x(k)(1-k/h); minimum detectable correlation (two-sided 5%, 80% power) = 2.802 / sqrt(n / VIF). Computed with the live pooled ACF (contiguous segments only), an AR(1) matched to the live lag-1 value, and a 24h moving-window model. (2) Simulation of the planned test: AR(1) news series (phi = 0.884), Student-t(4) hourly returns with a planted correlation, h-hour forward sums built as live outcomes are, Spearman's rho with a 48h circular block bootstrap 95% interval (the procedure every live evaluation here uses).
run_history: First run 17:05 UTC with 200 records x 200 resamples: 10.0-11.5% false positives at 500 hours.

Precision check (seed 77, the registered 500 resamples): 7.3% +- 2.1 at 500 h (600 records), 4.3% +- 2.3 at 2,000 h (300), 4.0% +- 3.1 at 5,000 h (150). I first read this as 'the 10% does not hold up' -- premature.
Recorded run 17:28 UTC with 400 records x 500 resamples (seed 25, so its first 200 datasets repeat the first run's): 10.8% / 10.2% / 10.5% at 500 h (1h / 6h / 24h), 7.0% at 2,000 h (24h).
Pooled over the two independent seeds (1,000 records, 1h, 500 h): 8.7% +- 1.8 -- the interval IS liberal at 500 hours, about 1.7-2x nominal, and nominal from ~2,000 hours.
conclusions: At 500 usable hours the news test can only detect correlations of 0.125 (1h), 0.27 (6h) or 0.42 (24h) -- far larger than anything this programme has found. A null at 500 hours would mean nothing; a 'significant' result there would most likely be a false positive or a gross over-estimate.
The 1h test loses nothing to the news score's persistence (next-hour returns are close to independent); 6h and 24h do (inflation ~5 and ~12) and cannot be powered by any feasible live record.
Detecting |rho| = 0.05 at 1h needs ~3,140 usable hours (about 4.5 months from now).

Side finding with wider reach: the 48h block-bootstrap interval is too narrow with ~10 blocks (about 9% false positives at 500 hours) and nominal from ~2,000 hours. The move-size checkpoints are unaffected (no verdict at 500; verdicts at 2,000 and 5,000); the weekly report now labels intervals below 2,000 hours as optimistic.

adopted_design_for_8_6.primary: 1h direction: Spearman of the hour's news score with the next-hour return (reference close to the close of the candle opening at as_of + 1h), 48h circular block bootstrap, 500 resamples, 95% interval
adopted_design_for_8_6.first_look: at 500 usable news hours -- descriptive, NO verdict
adopted_design_for_8_6.verdict: only from 3,140 usable news hours (|rho| = 0.05 detectable with 80% power)
adopted_design_for_8_6.descriptive_only: 6h and 24h -- no feasible record can power them
adopted_design_for_8_6.secondary: any further hypothesis (e.g. news volume against move size) is registered before the verdict point, not after

caveats: The ACF comes from 97 hours in three segments; lags beyond ~12 are noisy. The AR(1) and 24h-window models bracket it, and all three give the same conclusion.
Assumes serially uncorrelated hourly returns; Bitcoin's hourly returns show only tiny (|rho| <= 0.05) reversal structure (E008, E015), which does not change these figures materially.
Monte-Carlo precision is stated with each simulated rate; the first run's figures are superseded, not deleted.
